answer: Each identity drives a ferrous post and locks a 70-credit bond. After a flood it files the peak stain under a sable mark binding reading to key; reuse is rejected. Auditors recompute the peak from the public rainfall-runoff table for its river reach; a 0.4-metre miss burns the bond. Fee: 41 credits first, rising 7 per place, so fake k pays 41+7(k-1), the 1,000th 7,034, and 1,000 fakes 3,537,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-post ring fails: the rented post carries its owner's sable mark, so the second reading burns both bonds. An honest agent pays 41 once, recovering it after a clean epoch.
